sources.title: Optimal stabilization rate for the wave equation with hyperbolic boundary condition
sources.date_evidence: The retrieved title/front-matter passage identifies arXiv v1, 22 December 2025.
locators: Introduction discussion pointing to Section 3.2.2 trace estimates and Section 3.3 focusing modes
sources.supported_claim: The paper studies the wave equation on a smooth bounded domain of dimension at least two, with a damped hyperbolic boundary equation including a boundary Laplace–Beltrami term and optional disjoint static boundary component. Its reported 1/t stabilization result uses the geometric control condition and high-frequency resolvent/quasimode analysis. Retrieved passages emphasize separate normal/tangential trace estimates.
sources.relevance: Supports treating boundary inertia and derivative traces explicitly instead of inferring them from a bulk norm.
sources.transfer_limit: Long-time damped stabilization with surface propagation and geometric hypotheses does not supply the present finite-time, one-dimensional, time-dependent-potential, pointwise pulse certificate. No decay constant or trace theorem is imported.

sources.title: One dimensional wave equation with in-domain localized damping and Wentzell boundary conditions
sources.author_evidence: Full authorship was not present in the retained primary passages or search metadata used here.
sources.supported_claim: The displayed model has a positive Lipschitz spatial coefficient, nonnegative interior damping positive on a nonempty subinterval, and dynamic endpoint variables with positive constant coefficients. The abstract reports L2 and Lp stabilization/input-to-state methods. Retrieved Section 5 estimates control an integrated Lp bulk velocity/spatial-derivative quantity plus endpoint state variables.
sources.relevance: A one-dimensional structural neighbor for boundary oscillator variables and estimates driven by input terms.
sources.transfer_limit: Its localized damping and constant endpoint coefficients differ from the present HDB problem. The passages do not establish a uniform-in-time pointwise normal derivative error bound for a wave with our W(t,z), beta(t). The specific input-to-state theorem body was not among the returned passages, so no constants or exact theorem statement are inferred.

sources.title: Numerical integration in arbitrary-precision ball arithmetic
sources.date_evidence: The retrieved front matter identifies arXiv v1, 22 February 2018.
locators: Section 2, algorithm and implementation, direct-box step 2 and analytic-ellipse step 3
Section 3.2, endpoint singularities and infinite intervals
sources.supported_claim: The implementation combines rigorous direct interval-box enclosures and, where complex analyticity and an ellipse bound are verified, adaptive Gaussian quadrature. Endpoint/improper contributions require separate valid bounds when truncation is used.
sources.relevance: Supports explicit endpoint treatment and continuous-domain bounds rather than heuristic quadrature error estimates.
sources.transfer_limit: A smooth flat bump is not analytic across its support endpoints. The paper does not license an analytic Gaussian remainder across those endpoints. The current HDB implementation uses its own integer-dyadic outward arithmetic, exponential Taylor enclosure and real-cell range bounds; it is not an Arb run or a theorem imported from Arb.

sources.title: Certified and accurate computation of function space norms of deep neural networks
locators: Returned paper-index metadata and abstract only
sources.supported_claim: The returned abstract describes certified local interval boxes and adaptive aggregation for neural-network values/derivatives and norms, and cautions that finite point probes alone do not give guaranteed norm bounds without structure.
sources.relevance: A recent methodological comparison for continuous-cell certificates versus sample values.
sources.transfer_limit: The body and canonical authorship were not inspected. It concerns neural-network norms; our explicit bump calculation uses no neural network, and no result from this paper is used in the certificate.

scientific_scope: Literature comparison only. The HDB characteristic proof and integer/interval implementation require their own derivation, review and replay. This file proves neither their correctness nor scientific novelty.
